To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
muon bundles are a significant part of the muon component of horizontal cosmic rays and the muon bundle flux is not negligible at all, even for the highest energies.

the intensity of cosmic ray muon bundle in the energy range 10^14 – 10^16 eV is about 10% of that for single particles, and that the muon group flux near the horizon is about an order of magnitude greater than that of single muons.

the ratio of group intensity to the single particle intensity increases with increasing zenith angle, the number of muons in the group is larger than 5 for about 10% of events, the number of groups with more than 10 muons is about 1% for 60◦ < θ < 90◦.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of muon groups in horizontal cosmic ray muon flux at the Earth surface.
the development of the new experimental technique for studies of the muon component of cosmic rays in the atmosphere and in underground.
the study of the muon bundles with large multiplicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are consistent with the hypothesis of the primary composition being mainly protons, and the primary energy spectrum being a power law with a spectral index of about 2.7.
the experimental data are in a good agreement with MC simulation of the muon component of primary cosmic rays.
the muon bundles of large multiplicity are not observed in the horizontal component of cosmic rays at the Earth’s atmosphere.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the experimental data on muon bundles are in good agreement with the CORSIKA simulations.
we have shown that the DECOR detector can be used for the investigation of the muon component in the horizontal direction.
the experimental results are in a good agreement with CORSIKA predictions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the experimental data are consistent with CORSIKA predictions for the energy region 1017 – 1019 eV.
there is a large fraction of muon groups of high multiplicity in the range of 60◦ – 70◦, which is not predicted by the CORSIKA model.
the muon group intensity is not constant for all zenith angles and the ratio of muons in bundles to that of single particles increases with zenith angle.
